traps.snippet:
MERGE dw.dim_policy AS tgt
        USING #src AS src
           ON tgt.policy_id = src.policy_id
          AND tgt.is_current = 'Y'
        WHEN MATCHED AND (   ISNULL(src.status, '')        <> ISNULL(tgt.status, '')
                          OR ISNULL(src.broker_code, '')   <> ISNULL(tgt.broker_co…
traps.note: This MERGE closes the current version of changed policies (valid_to = snapshot - 1, is_current = 'N'). Spark has to rebuild the whole dimension from its previous state and the batch.
The status <> check is case-insensitive, so a change of letter case only (e.g. 'Active' to 'ACTIVE') opens no new version in legacy. Spark would open one.
The status <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a change in trailing spaces alone does not close the version in legacy.
The status change check uses ISNULL(..., ''), so a NULL status and '' count as equal and no new version opens.
The broker_code <> check is case-insensitive, so a broker code that changes only in letter case does not trigger a new version in legacy.
The broker_code <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a code that differs only by trailing spaces does not count as a change.

The broker_code change check treats NULL and '' as the same value. Also, the source side has already been truncated to 'DIRECT-SAL' by the ISNULL at line 95, and Spark must compare against that truncated value.
ISNULL(annual_premium, 0) treats a NULL premium and 0 as equal, so that difference opens no new version.
The vehicle_reg <> check is case-insensitive, so a registration that changes only in case ('ab12cde' to 'AB12CDE') is not a change in legacy.
The vehicle_reg <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a registration with added trailing spaces is not seen as changed.
vehicle_reg is nullable. ISNULL(..., '') makes NULL and '' equal, so moving between NULL and empty opens no new version. Spark null-safe comparisons would treat it as a change.

defects.title: Row-multiplying joins / duplicate snapshot rows create duplicate current versions
defects.description: #src is built from stg.policy_snapshots joined to stg.products, stg.brokers and dw.dim_customer, and nothing makes it unique per policy_id. If a staging table has a duplicate key (the _row_seq column suggests re-staged rows), or a policy appears twice in one snapshot, #src gets several rows for the policy. The INSERT's NOT EXISTS check only looks at rows already in the table, so every duplicate is opened as another current version (is_current='Y'), which counts its annual_premium twice. On a later snapshot those duplicates can also make the MERGE fail because it tries to update the same target row more than once.
defects.intended_behaviour: Exactly one current version per policy_id per snapshot: each lookup returns at most one row per key, and the snapshot is reduced to one row per policy_id (for example the latest _row_seq) before the MERGE/INSERT.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(annual_premium), 0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT g.annual_premium, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g.policy_id, g.source_snapshot_date ORDER BY g.policy_sk) AS rn FROM golden_dw_dim_policy g) x WHERE rn > 1

defects.title: Policies missing from a later snapshot are never closed
defects.description: The MERGE only has a WHEN MATCHED branch. A policy that is in dim_policy but missing from the new snapshot (lapsed, purged or moved out) keeps is_current='Y' and valid_to=9999-12-31 for ever, so it is still reported as a live current policy.
defects.intended_behaviour: Close the current version (valid_to = snapshot date - 1, is_current = 'N') when a policy no longer appears in the snapshot, for example with WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE AND tgt.is_current = 'Y'.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(g.annual_premium), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_policy g WHERE g.is_current = 'Y' AND g.source_snapshot_date < DATE'2025-12-31' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stg_policy_snapshots s WHERE s.snapshot_date = DATE'2025-12-31' AND s.policy_id = g.policy_id)

defects.title: Inner join to stg.products silently drops policies with an unknown product
defects.description: stg.products is joined with an INNER JOIN. Any policy whose product_code is missing from the product register is left out of #src with no warning, so it never gets a dimension row, or is never versioned if it already has one.
defects.intended_behaviour: Keep every policy in the snapshot (LEFT JOIN with a default or unknown product) or reject/log the unmatched rows. The dimension is meant to hold every policy term.

tests.description: Letter-case variants across two runs (2025-06-30, then 2025-12-31). Policy 1001 has product_code 'motor01' and the product register has 'MOTOR01'. The legacy inner join still matches it; a binary Spark join drops the policy. Policy 1002 has broker 'brk001' and the register has 'BRK001'. Legacy finds the broker_name; Spark leaves it NULL. In run 2 the changes are case-only: 1001 status 'Active' to 'ACTIVE', 1002 broker 'brk001' to 'BRK001', 1003 vehicle_reg 'ab12cde' to 'AB12CDE'. Legacy opens no new version for these; Spark would close and reopen each one. Policy 1004 is the control: its status really changes, to 'Lapsed'.

Trailing spaces and CHAR padding across two runs. Policy 2001 has product_code 'MOTOR01 ' with a trailing space. The legacy inner join keeps it; Spark drops the policy. Its broker 'BRK1' matches the CHAR(6) register code 'BRK1  ', which is stored padded. Legacy finds the broker_name; Spark gets NULL. Customers 501 and 503 have CHAR(4) segment codes 'GO' and 'STD', which legacy pads to 'GO  ' and 'STD '; Spark leaves them unpadded. Customer 502's 'PLAT' is the canonical 4-character code. In run 2 the only changes are trailing spaces: 2001 status 'Active  ', 2002 broker 'BRK002 ', 2003 vehicle_reg 'CD34EFG  '. Legacy opens no new version for these; Spark would. Policy 2004 is the control: its premium really changes.

ISNULL behaviour across two runs. Policies 3001 and 3004 (run 1) and 3005 (new in run 2) have a NULL broker_code. ISNULL takes the VARCHAR(10) type of p.broker_code, so legacy stores 'DIRECT-SAL'; a Spark coalesce writes 'DIRECT-SALES'. 3001 stays NULL in run 2. Legacy compares 'DIRECT-SAL' with 'DIRECT-SAL' and opens no version. A Spark job that compares the full literal against the stored value, or that mixes the two, can flag a change. 3002 moves vehicle_reg from NULL to '', and 3003 from '' to NULL. Under ISNULL(...,'') these are equal and no version opens; a null-safe Spark compare would open one. 3004 is the control: its broker really changes, from NULL to BRK001. NULL status or premium cannot be tested here because both columns are NOT NULL in staging.

lineage agent notes: dw.dim_policy is both an input and the output: the job never truncates it. The MERGE closes changed current versions by setting valid_to = @SnapshotDate - 1 and is_current = 'N'. The INSERT then opens a new version for policies that have no current row left. The change test compares the snapshot with the current row on status, broker_code (after ISNULL to 'DIRECT-SALES'), annual_premium and vehicle_reg. It is listed as filters from both sides because it decides which rows get closed and re-versioned.

product_code comes from pr.product_code, which always equals p.product_code because of the inner join. The LEFT JOIN keys to stg.brokers and dw.dim_customer don't remove rows, but they could duplicate them, so I gave them lower confidence as filters.

stg.brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6) while p.broker_code is VARCHAR(10). The join therefore matches only codes of 6 characters or fewer, because SQL Server ignores trailing spaces when comparing. Spark comparisons don't ignore trailing spaces, so the migrated join should trim or pad the codes.

The @last_loaded guard stops the whole run (THROW) instead of filtering rows. It's listed as a low-confidence filter on source_snapshot_date.

The script drops and recreates dw.dim_policy on deploy (lines 29-57). That is DDL, not part of the procedure's run.

ORDER BY s.policy_id on the INSERT changes only the order in which IDENTITY values are assigned to policy_sk. It doesn't decide which rows appear. To match policy_sk values, the migration must reproduce that order.

warnings:
translator notes: Points for the reviewer:

1. load_ts: the legacy uses SYSDATETIME(); I use F.localtimestamp(). It is one constant per run, but it can never match the legacy wall-clock time, so exclude it from reconciliation.

2. MERGE duplicate check: the job raises an error when more than one source row that meets the change condition matches the same current target row. This is meant to mirror SQL Server error 8672. I assumed matches that open no new version (they fail the WHEN MATCHED AND condition) do not count. Please confirm.

3. policy_sk: it continues from max(previous policy_sk) + row_number() in policy_id order. I assumed no identity values were lost to rolled-back inserts. Ties on a duplicated policy_id are broken by the _row_seq of stg.policy_snapshots, then stg.products, then stg.brokers. dw.dim_customer has no _row_seq.

4. Text comparisons (product and broker joins, the is_current filters, the status / broker_code / vehicle_reg change checks) use upper(rtrim(...)). Stored values stay unchanged.

5. Padding: customer_segment is padded with rpad to 4 and currency to 3 (both CHAR outputs). This is also applied to carried-over history, and is harmless when it is already padded.

6. Errors: the INC-2105 later-snapshot guard and the empty-snapshot THROW raise a RuntimeError. They use collect-style actions (first / isEmpty).
